newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANY'S SAMMER IS HEIR TO BECKENBAUER'S MANTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY'S SAMMER IS HEIR TO BECKENBAUER'S MANTLE.

text.p: The 1996 European championship was perhaps the final proof that in Matthias Sammer Germany have at last found a libero worthy of the pioneer of the role, "Kaiser" Franz Beckenbauer.
Sammer, named the winner of the Golden Boot award on Monday, was one of Germany's best players of the tournament in England.
He not only marshalled the back row but turned defence into attack with lightning speed and contributed two crucial goals to get his side out of trouble and steer them to the title.
Appropriately, Beckenbauer himself was on hand to offer the highest tribute.

"He plays this role perfectly. It's instinctive. He always does the right thing at the right moment," said the man who inspired the Germans to their 1974 World Cup triumph as captain and made them world champions again as coach in 1990.

The red-haired, 29-year-old Sammer already had a special place in his nation's soccer history as the first former East German to play for Germany after unification in 1990. Sammer has now earned 48 caps to go with the 23 he won for East Germany.
Along with midfielder Andreas Moeller, he forms the hub of a Borussia Dortmund side which has won two straight Bundesliga titles and could yet snatch a third.

Despite often being under instructions at Dortmund to rein in his natural attacking tendency, he scores in the league at around one goal every four games -- a formidable record for a player who is also no shrinking violet in the tackle.
If he has a weakness, it is a hot-headed temperament which occasionally gets him into trouble with the referees he harangues a shade too often.
Sammer, who had spells with VfB Stuttgart and Internazionale Milan before moving to Dortmund, admits he becomes a different person when he walks on to a soccer pitch.
"When I'm relaxing in an armchair at home and see myself on television, I do think: 'My God, are you crazy?' I can understand people who say Sammer's got a screw loose."
